summary: Jonathan C. Gold works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He taught at the University of Vermont, served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at Drew University (attested 2006), and was appointed Assistant Professor at Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral work at Harvard University (~1975–1984) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

Jonathan Geen is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed his doctorate under Phyllis Granoff at McMaster University by 2001. He has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher educated at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1960–1963). He served as a fellow and tutor at New College, Oxford (~1967–1996), held a post at King's College London (~1996–2013), and became a Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford (~2013).

Philosopher Jonathan Lear studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Rockefeller University (Ph.D. ~1973–1978). He held posts at Clare College, Cambridge (~1978–1985), Yale (1978–1996), Cambridge (1979–1985), and the University of Chicago (2014–2022) as John U. Nef Distinguished Service Professor.

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer works in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the University of California, Berkeley (BA ~1971–1983), he became the George F. Dales Jr. & Barbara A. Dales Professor of Anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1985).

Religious studies scholar Jonathan Z. Smith earned degrees from Haverford and Yale. After positions at Dartmouth and UC Santa Barbara, he served at the University of Chicago (~1968–2013), including as Dean of the College (1977–1982) and Distinguished Service Professor.

Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at International Buddhist University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg in 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongcheol Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Seoul National University and earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (1994) under Ekyo Ejima, later holding posts at the University of Mysore (1992) and the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2001).

Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Yonsei, Seoul National University, and UCLA (MA 1994) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., later serving as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Ryukoku University (~1939–1950). He spent his academic career there from 1950, serving as lecturer, assistant professor, and professor emeritus (1970–1989), alongside leadership roles in several research institutes.

Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist who studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University, earning his doctorate under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink (~1987–1993). He became an associate professor at Leiden University in 1993.

Josef Horovitz worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctorate under Eduard Sachau (~1895–1898) and held a post at Goethe University Frankfurt from around 1914 to 1931.

Josef Schick, a scholar of Indology, studied at Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD 1887–1889). He taught at Berlin, Bonn, and Heidelberg before serving as an ordentlicher Professor at the University of Munich from 1896 to 1925.

Josef Strzygowski was an art historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Munich (~1882–1885). He held academic posts at the University of Graz (~1892–1909), the University of Vienna (~1909–1933), and Åbo Akademi University (~1925).
Josef van Ess was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Bonn (~1953–1959) and held a post at the University of Tübingen from around 1968 to 1999.

Joseph Andrew Sittler was a religious studies scholar who studied at Wittenberg University (~1923–1927). He taught at the Lutheran School of Theology at Chicago (~1943–1957) and served as professor of theology at the University of Chicago (1957–1973).

Joseph Campbell was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Columbia University (~1925–1927) and studied in Paris and Munich. After a post at Canterbury School (1933), he taught at Sarah Lawrence College from 1934 to 1972.
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

Joseph Dalton Hooker studied at the University of Glasgow (~1832–1839). After working at the British Geological Survey (1845–1847), he served at the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew (1847–1885), where he was Director from around 1865 to 1885.
